text: Study Sources 1 and 2.

‘It is easy to use less energy in your home.’
What are the strengths and weaknesses of the argument supporting this claim?

or methods you might use.

text: Study Source 3.

parts.text: Identify one fact from Dhia’s statement. Explain why this is a fact.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Arif is arguing that we need to use less energy.

parts.label: (i)
parts.text: Identify one prediction from Arif’s statement.

parts.label: (ii)
parts.text: Explain how well this prediction supports Arif’s argument.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
Which argument is more convincing, Dhia’s or Arif’s?
Your answer should consider both arguments and you should support your point of view with
their words.
You should also consider:
• the strength of their reasoning and evidence
• their use of language
• the different kinds of information used.

text: Study Source 4.
A government wants to take action to protect the environment.
The following actions are being considered:
• generate more electricity from solar and wind power
• encourage people to use less electricity in their home
• educate people about the causes of climate change.
Which one of these actions would you recommend to the government, and why?
In your answer, you should:
• state your recommendation
• give reasons and evidence to support your choice
• use the material in the sources and/or any of your own ideas
• consider different arguments and perspectives.
